thread:
jess: heads up — ran into a weird issue with RN webview + hosted API streaming. streaming init returns 200 but then we get a 401 in the middle when the token rotates. anyone seen this pattern?

raj: yep — common when ephemeral tokens are short-lived and the client doesn't reattach headers for an already-open stream. web sockets / fetch streams don't resend headers on reconnect.

mia: what auth flow are you using? our mobile SDK uses a refresh token flow to mint short-lived bearer tokens for the webview bridge.

jess: using server-side ephemeral tokens (TTL 60s) passed to the webview via query param: https://inference.redwood/example?token=XXX then the webview opens an EventSource to /stream. Works initially but after ~30–50s the stream fails with 401 and never recovers.

leo: EventSource doesn't support custom headers, so query param is the usual workaround, but CORS preflight + SameSite cookies get weird. Are you sending Access-Control-Allow-Credentials?

jess: we set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://our-app.com and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on the API. EventSource still gets 401 mid-stream. logs show: "auth: token expired" from gateway.

raj: two things to check: 1) token TTL and clock skew — mobile might be behind; 2) is there a transparent refresh flow? If the webview can't re-open with a fresh token, you need a server-side long-lived session and the server reenacts the stream.

mia: for RN specifically, we've shifted to embedding a tiny bridge that handles token rotation. flow: native obtains ephemeral token, injects it into webview via postMessage before creating EventSource, and listens for a "refreshNeeded" message from web layer to request a new token.

jess: any code snippets for that bridge? our team is iOS + Android.

mia: simplified RN pattern: 

```
// RN side
const token = await getEphemeralToken();
webview.postMessage(JSON.stringify({type: 'setToken', token}));

// in the webview app
window.addEventListener('message', e => {
  const msg = JSON.parse(e.data);
  if (msg.type === 'setToken') startEventSource(msg.token);
});
```

StartEventSource attaches token to query string, and when native sees stream error it requests a new token and posts it in.

leo: for native Swift/Kotlin wrappers (not webview), prefer using a short polling keepalive that checks token TTL and refreshes proactively before it expires. don't wait for 401 because streaming APIs often won't auto-replay.

jess: question: is passing token in query param acceptable security-wise? security says ephemeral + TLS OK but i'm worried about logs and referer.

raj: ephemeral tokens mitigate long-term risk. also set Referrer-Policy and avoid exposing token in links. You can also use ephemeral signed cookies with SameSite=None + Secure if you control webview headers. But EventSource + cookies is tricky because some webviews don't send cookies consistently.

mia: another approach is WebSocket with a one-time auth handshake. WS supports initial headers (or subprotocol) then you can renew by initiating a new WS connection and gracefully swapping streams — but that requires app-level migration logic.

jess: hmm, we prefer to keep SSE for simplicity. Is there a recommended TTL? 60s seems too short.

leo: 5–15 minutes is more pragmatic for SSE unless you have strict security/regulatory constraints. If you want to keep 60s, you must implement a robust token refresh handshake between native and web layer.

mia: also watch for backgrounding: iOS suspends webviews and background refresh won't run. For long-lived streams we recommend moving streaming to native layer (URLSession/OkHttp) and only mirror events into the webview via postMessage.

jess: ok — one more: CORS preflight keeps failing intermittently on Android webview with OPTIONS 403. any quick fixes?

raj: make sure OPTIONS handling is allowed for the exact Origin header sent by the webview — some Android webviews send "file://" or an empty origin. If origin is missing, treat it as allowed in our gateway config or normalize on client to set a consistent origin via meta tags.

leo: another gotcha: some embed layers add custom user agents that break our origin matching. Logs should show the Origin header — check gateway logs.

ci-bot: deploy status: gateway CORS config rolled out to staging at 1769812200. No errors reported after the change. :white_check_mark:

jess: thanks! Actions for me: increase TTL for staging to 10m, add native bridge token-refresh flow for webview, and file an issue to consider WS-based streaming in the mobile SDK.

mia: ping me when you have a repro — I can help wire the RN bridge.

raj: also add server-side idempotent resume tokens: include a resume_id on stream start so client can reconnect and continue the session if a short 401 occurs.

jess: good idea. logging note: include ephemeral token hash in logs (not token) so we can correlate without leaking secrets. :lock: :thumbsup:
